items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1958-Fall
items.q: I think it was Mudd Carey, they quote him as saying blues, and they said only the ignorant played blues.

ctx.x: Why shouldn't he tell the term of that? He's probably talking about Ammons and Johnson.

It might have been Ammons and Johnson, or Johnson and Turner. Who was it? There's a couple of them that were playing around New York. Yeah, they were around. Anyhow, the guys that only know one, too. That's what got it with Handy, too, you know. Because Handy hadn't really done something with it. The blues made plenty of money out of it. Johnny said, blues wasn't considered music in those days, which was a fact. They'd hush you up as you started playing it down there and go on and that kind of thing. And also, I…
You hear about the Bolden band playing ragtime. I wonder what they mean by that.
